# Test fixtures

Three directories, for three different reasons.

## `test/fixtures/`

Committed, hand-placed. Currently one file:

- `libheif-2x2-single.heic` — a 471-byte single-item HEIC from libheif's
  `heif-enc`. Small, non-Apple, and it happens to carry a real `clap` property
  (the frame is coded 64×64 and cropped to 2×2), which makes it the crop test.

## `test/fixtures/generated/`

Committed, reproducible. Rebuild with:

```sh
sh tools/make-fixtures.sh
```

An asymmetric test pattern — every corner differs, plus a directional wedge — so
a wrong rotation or a flipped mirror axis is obvious rather than subtle. Encoded
once, then forged into transform variants by `tools/inject-property.ts`, which
adds an `irot` or `imir` property to an existing file and fixes up the `iloc`
offsets that shift as a result.

No encoder available to us writes `imir`, and the axis semantics are the single
most commonly inverted detail in HEIF implementations, so these fixtures exist
specifically to settle it by measurement. See the note in
`src/render/transform.ts`.

These are 10-bit, which also covers the 10-bit path.

## `test/fixtures/local/` — gitignored

A personal photo corpus. **Not committed**, because these are real photographs of
real people.

The manifest and both test suites load this directory when it is present and skip
it silently when it is not, so a local run is far more thorough than CI without
anyone having to publish their photo library.

To populate it, drop HEIC files in and run:

```sh
node --experimental-strip-types tools/make-manifest.ts test/fixtures/local
for f in test/fixtures/local/*.[hH][eE][iI][cC]; do
  heif-convert -q 100 "$f" "${f%.*}.ref.png"
done
```

### CI coverage is weaker than local coverage, on purpose

CI runs against the committed fixtures only. That means CI does **not** exercise
real Apple grid images across device generations, which is where container
parsing bugs actually live.

If you want CI to cover that, commit a handful of real iPhone photos you are
comfortable publishing — ideally spanning several models, both orientations, and
at least one 90/270-rotated file — and add them to `test/fixtures/`.

## Manifests

`manifest.json` in each directory holds the expectations. It is generated from
libheif's `heif-info` and from `exiftool`, never from this package's own parser:
a manifest generated by the code under test asserts nothing.

Note that `heif-info` reports dimensions and tile layout in **display**
orientation, so a 90/270 rotation swaps both relative to the coded image. The
manifest generator accounts for this.
